Mocking One More Prisma Call

createComment now queries Prisma twice, not once — comment.service.test.js's mocks grow to match, or the recipient-resolution code has nothing to run against.

comment.service.js's createComment does more work now than it did in Week 3 — it looks the parent ticket up a second time to resolve recipients (Topic 3) before ever emitting ticket.commented. A test suite mocking Prisma has to mock that call too, or the code under test crashes reading properties off undefined before it ever reaches the assertion:

// Figure 5.17: two more Prisma calls to mock, matching the new recipient lookup (tests/unit/comment.service.test.js, excerpt)
const mockPrisma = {
  ticket: { findUnique: jest.fn() },
  comment: { create: jest.fn() /* ...other methods unchanged... */ },
  user: { findMany: jest.fn() },
};

it('createComment never notifies the comment author, even if they are the customer', async () => {
  mockPrisma.comment.create.mockResolvedValue({ id: 2, ticketId: 7, authorId: 13, body: 'Thanks!' });
  mockPrisma.ticket.findUnique.mockResolvedValue({ id: 7, subject: 'Cannot log in', customerId: 13, watchers: [] });

  await createComment(7, { body: 'Thanks!', authorId: 13 });

  expect(mockPrisma.user.findMany).not.toHaveBeenCalled();
  expect(emitSpy).toHaveBeenCalledWith(EVENTS.TICKET_COMMENTED, expect.objectContaining({ recipients: [] }));
});

This test is picking out exactly the edge case Topic 3's Set-based exclusion exists for: the comment's author is the ticket's customer here (customerId: 13, authorId: 13), so the right outcome is zero recipients and no wasted user.findMany call at all — not "notify the customer, then filter them out later." comments.routes.test.js, the integration test sitting on top of this same service through a real route, needed the exact same two additions — ticket.findUnique and user.findMany mocks — for the same reason: any test exercising createComment now runs through Topic 3's recipient-resolution path whether or not that test cares about notifications at all.

That's the practical cost of Topic 3's decision to resolve recipients inside the service rather than in each listener — the tests around that service have to know about one more query. It's a trade this project accepts deliberately: three listener files that never touch Prisma for this at all, against one service function whose tests need two more mocks.
